examples.en: Jeju Island is famous for its tangerines.
In winter I buy tangerines by the box and eat them.

examples.ko: 감귤 껍질을 말려서 차로 마시기도 해요.
examples.en: People also dry tangerine peel and drink it as tea.
This tangerine is sweet and juicy.
The farmers are busy picking tangerines.
The tangerine juice I got as a gift was delicious.

explain: 집에서는 보통 '귤'이라고 하고, '감귤'은 귤류를 모두 가리키거나 제주도 특산물을 말할 때 많이 써요. '오렌지'는 수입 과일이라는 느낌이 강하고 '귤'보다 커요. 겨울에 손으로 까서 먹는 과일은 '귤'이에요.

phrases.en: In winter I eat a lot of tangerines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 말할 때 더 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easier word people use more at home.

phrases.en: I visited a mandarin orange farm in Jeju.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귤을 키우는 곳을 말할 때 '감귤'을 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 감귤 is often used for places where citrus is grown.

phrases.en: In autumn I picked mandarin oranges with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무에서 열매를 딸 때 '따다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 따다 is the verb for picking fruit from a tree.

explain_en: At home people just say 귤, while 감귤 covers the whole citrus family or comes up with Jeju specialties. 오렌지 feels like an imported, bigger fruit. The little peel-by-hand fruit eaten in winter is 귤.

en: to be voracious; to be gluttonous

examples.ko: 동생은 배가 고파서 밥을 게걸스럽게 먹었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling was hungry and ate the meal greedily.

examples.ko: 게걸스러운 모습이 부끄러워서 조금 천천히 먹었어요.
examples.en: I was embarrassed by how greedily I was eating, so I slowed down a bit.

examples.ko: 아이가 빵 먹는 모습이 좀 게걸스러워 보여요.
examples.en: The way the child eats bread looks a bit gluttonous.

examples.ko: 어제 너무 게걸스러웠다는 생각에 오늘은 적게 먹었어요.
examples.en: I felt I had been too gluttonous yesterday, so I ate less today.

examples.ko: 게걸스러워서 같이 밥 먹기 불편하다는 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: I was told it's uncomfortable to eat together because of the greedy way I eat.

examples.ko: 게걸스럽지 않게 예의 바르게 먹는 법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned how to eat politely without looking greedy.

explain: 보기 싫을 만큼 욕심내서 먹는 모습에 써서 칭찬이 아니라 흉보는 느낌이에요. '허겁지겁'은 급하게 먹는 모양이고, '게걸스럽다'는 탐욕스럽게 먹는 느낌이 더 강해요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '게걸스러워요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: The hungry child eats the bread greedily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹는 모습을 말할 때 '-게'로 바꿔 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common phrase, changing it to -게 to describe how someone eats.

phrases.en: The way he eats is a bit gluttonous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '게걸스러워요'가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is a ㅂ-irregular, so it becomes 게걸스러워요.

phrases.en: I was late, so I wolfed down food and left.
phrases.nuance_ko: 급해서 서두르는 모양이에요. '게걸스럽다'는 탐욕스러운 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This describes hurrying because of urgency, while 게걸스럽다 feels more greedy.

explain_en: It describes eating so greedily that it looks unpleasant, so it is critical rather than praise. '허겁지겁' just means eating in a hurry, while '게걸스럽다' feels more greedy. It is a 'ㅂ' irregular, so it becomes '게걸스러워요'.

examples.ko: 복숭아를 한 입 베어 물자 과즙이 줄줄 흘렀어요.
examples.en: When I bit into the peach, the juice ran down.

examples.ko: 이 젤리는 진짜 과즙을 넣어서 만들었대요.
examples.en: I heard this jelly is made with real fruit juice.

examples.ko: 고기를 레몬 과즙에 잠깐 재워 두세요.
examples.en: Marinate the meat in lemon juice for a little while.

examples.ko: 이 주스는 설탕 없이 과즙만으로 만들었어요.
examples.en: This juice is made with fruit juice alone, without sugar.

examples.ko: 과즙 가득한 포도를 한 송이나 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate a whole bunch of juicy grapes.

examples.ko: 과즙으로 얼룩진 옷은 바로 빨아야 지워져요.
examples.en: Clothes stained with fruit juice come clean only if you wash them right away.

explain: '주스'는 마시는 음료 전체를 말하고, '과즙'은 과일에서 나오는 즙 자체를 말해요. 포장지에 '과즙 10%'처럼 쓰여 있어서 얼마나 들어 있는지 알 수 있어요. 과일이 즙이 많을 때 '과즙이 풍부하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: This tangerine is full of juice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과일에 즙이 많을 때 쓰는 대표적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical expression for fruit with lots of juice.

phrases.example: 한 입 먹자 과즙이 입안에서 터졌어요.
phrases.en: The juice burst in my mouth with one bite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물기 많은 과일을 먹을 때의 느낌을 생생하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Vividly describes the feeling of eating a juicy fruit.

phrases.en: This drink is 10% fruit juice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포장지에서 과일 즙이 얼마나 들었는지 알려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used on packaging to show how much fruit juice is in it.

explain_en: '주스' means the drink as a whole, while '과즙' is the juice that comes from the fruit itself. Packaging says things like '과즙 10%' to show how much is in it. When a fruit is very juicy, people say '과즙이 풍부하다'.

examples.ko: 저녁 먹기 전에 군것질을 하면 밥맛이 없어요.
examples.en: If I snack before dinner, I lose my appetite.
I bought snacks to nibble on at the cinema.
Children really love snacking.
I gained weight because of snacking.
I keep snacking while studying for exams.
I went to the market to buy some snacks.

explain: 밥 먹는 시간이 아닐 때 과자나 간식을 이것저것 먹는 일이에요. '간식'은 먹는 음식 자체를 가리키지만 '군것질'은 먹는 행동에 가까워요. 먹고 싶어서 자꾸 입에 넣는 느낌이 있어서 '군것질을 끊다', '군것질을 줄이다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: If you snack at night, you gain weight.
phrases.nuance_ko: '군것질'에 '하다'를 붙여 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 turns it into the action of snacking.

phrases.en: I quit snacking for my health.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 습관을 그만둘 때 '끊다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 끊다 is used for quitting a bad habit.

phrases.en: I put some snacks in my travel bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거리'가 붙으면 군것질로 먹을 음식이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 거리, it means food meant for snacking.

explain_en: It means eating snacks here and there outside mealtimes. '간식' can refer to the food itself, while '군것질' is closer to the act of snacking. It carries a feel of nibbling out of habit, as in '군것질을 끊다' and '군것질을 줄이다'.

examples.ko: 더운 날에는 미숫가루를 물에 타 마셔요.
examples.en: On hot days I mix misugaru with water and drink it.
I added milk to the misugaru, and it tastes nutty.
This is misugaru my grandmother made herself.

examples.ko: 미숫가루는 한 끼 대신 먹기도 해요.
examples.en: Some people have misugaru instead of a meal.
Would you like a glass of misugaru?
Misugaru clumps, so you have to stir it well.

explain: 곡식을 가루로 만든 것을 찬물이나 우유에 타서 마시는 음식이에요. '미싯가루'라고 잘못 쓰는 일이 많은데, 표준 표기는 '미숫가루'예요.

phrases.en: I mixed misugaru into milk and drank it for breakfast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미숫가루를 물이나 우유에 섞어 마실 때 '타다'라고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '타다' is the verb for mixing misugaru into water or milk to drink.
phrases.en_equiv: to mix misugaru into a drink

phrases.example: 더운 여름에는 미숫가루 한 잔이 최고예요.
phrases.en: In hot summer, a glass of misugaru is the best.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마시는 양을 셀 때 '한 잔'을 붙여요. 주문하거나 권할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '한 잔' to count a serving. It is common when ordering or offering a drink.

phrases.example: 이 집 미숫가루 맛이 정말 고소해요.
phrases.en: This place's misugaru tastes really nutty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음료의 맛을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for describing how the drink tastes.

explain_en: It is a powder of ground grains that you mix into cold water or milk to drink. Many people misspell it as '미싯가루', but the standard spelling is '미숫가루'.

examples.en: An eel is a long, slippery fish.
I ate grilled eel as a summer health food.
A big eel is swimming in the aquarium.

examples.ko: 뱀장어 요리를 파는 식당이 근처에 있어요.
examples.en: There is a restaurant nearby that sells eel dishes.
I saw a live eel at the market.
I caught a fish that looks similar to an eel.

explain: 식당에서는 보통 '장어'로 줄여 불러요. 장어라고 부르는 물고기에는 다른 종류도 있어요. '장어구이', '장어덮밥'처럼 요리 이름에 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: I like eel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당이나 일상 대화에서는 뱀장어를 보통 이렇게 줄여 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: In restaurants and daily talk, 뱀장어 is usually shortened to this.

phrases.en: Do you want to have grilled eel for dinner tonight?
phrases.nuance_ko: 구워서 먹는 요리 이름이라서 식당에서 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the grilled dish, often seen in restaurants.

phrases.en: I caught an eel in the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물고기를 직접 잡는 이야기에 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about catching the fish yourself.

explain_en: At restaurants it is usually shortened to '장어'. Other kinds of fish are also called 장어. It often appears in dish names such as '장어구이' and '장어덮밥'.

examples.en: I bought one dried pollack at the market.
I soaked the dried pollack in water and made soup.

examples.ko: 새 차를 사면 북어를 달아 두는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people hang dried pollack in a new car.
I pounded the dried pollack with a mallet to soften it.
Mom is peeling the skin off the dried pollack.

examples.ko: 북어는 오래 보관할 수 있어서 집에 늘 있어요.
examples.en: Dried pollack keeps for a long time, so we always have some at home.

explain: 같은 명태라도 상태에 따라 이름이 달라요. 얼리면 '동태', 겨울에 얼렸다 말리면 '황태', 그냥 바싹 말린 것은 '북어'라고 해요. 딱딱해서 방망이로 두드려 부드럽게 한 뒤에 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I pounded the dried pollack with a club to soften it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리하기 전에 딱딱한 북어를 부드럽게 만드는 과정이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The step of softening hard dried pollack before cooking.

phrases.en: I made seasoned shredded dried pollack and ate it with rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 북어를 가늘게 찢거나 썬 것이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Dried pollack that is torn or cut into thin strips.

phrases.en: Hwangtae is softer than bugeo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 명태지만 겨울에 얼렸다 말린 것이라 북어와 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also pollack, but frozen and dried over winter, so it differs from 북어.

explain_en: The same pollack gets different names depending on how it is treated: frozen is '동태', freeze-dried over winter is '황태', and simply dried hard is '북어'. It is so stiff that people often pound it with a mallet to soften it before cooking.

examples.en: Put the meat on once the grill is hot enough.

examples.ko: 고기 굽는 불판을 새로 닦아 주세요.
examples.en: Please wipe down the grill used for cooking the meat.

examples.ko: 불판 위에서 김치가 지글지글 익고 있어요.
examples.en: Kimchi is sizzling on the grill.

examples.ko: 고기를 올리기 전에 불판에 기름을 먼저 두르세요.
examples.en: Before putting on the meat, first coat the grill with oil.

examples.ko: 불판 때문에 옷에 냄새가 많이 뱄어요.
examples.en: The smell from the grill soaked into my clothes.
Each grill has a small vent attached.

explain: 고깃집에서 고기를 굽는 판을 말할 때 자주 써요. 그물 모양인 '석쇠'와는 다르게 판 형태를 떠올리면 돼요. '불판을 갈아 주세요'는 식당에서 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: Boss, could you change the grill, please?
phrases.nuance_ko: 고깃집에서 불판이 탔을 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often said at a BBQ restaurant when the grill has burned.

phrases.en: Please put the meat on the grill.
phrases.nuance_ko: '위에'를 붙여 고기를 놓는 위치를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '위에' says where the meat is placed.

phrases.en: The meat stuck to the grill, so it's hard to remove.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 판에 붙어 타는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when food sticks to the pan and burns.

explain_en: It is often used at barbecue restaurants for the plate the meat is cooked on. Unlike a '석쇠' (a mesh grill), picture a flat plate. '불판을 갈아 주세요' is a handy phrase to use at a restaurant.

examples.en: This vegetable is tasty even when eaten raw.

examples.ko: 저는 생선을 생으로 먹는 게 아직 무서워요.
examples.en: I'm still afraid of eating fish raw.
It's fine to blend carrots raw and drink them.
I ate garlic raw, and now my stomach burns.

examples.ko: 과일은 생으로 먹는 게 몸에 좋다고 해요.
examples.en: They say eating fruit raw is good for your body.

examples.ko: 버섯은 생으로 먹지 말고 꼭 익혀서 드세요.
examples.en: Don't eat mushrooms raw; be sure to cook them first.

explain: 익히거나 가공하지 않고 그대로라는 뜻으로 '먹다, 갈다, 마시다'와 자주 써요. 반대로 익힌 경우는 '익혀서', '삶아서'처럼 말하고, '날것'은 명사이고 '생으로'는 먹는 방법을 말해요.

phrases.en: Carrots are sweet even when eaten raw.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이에요. 익히지 않고 그대로 먹는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, meaning to eat something uncooked.

phrases.en: I blend the fruit raw to make juice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 익히지 않고 그대로 갈아서 쓴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means blending something without cooking it first.

phrases.example: 이 생선은 날것으로 먹을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can eat this fish raw.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 '날것'은 명사라서 '으로'를 붙여 방법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning; '날것' is a noun, so '으로' marks the way it is eaten.

explain_en: It means as it is, without cooking or processing, and is often used with '먹다', '갈다' and '마시다'. For the opposite you say '익혀서' or '삶아서'; '날것' is a noun, while '생으로' describes the way you eat something.

examples.en: My grandmother made yakgwa for us during the holiday.

examples.ko: 약과는 달고 쫀득해서 차와 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: Yakgwa is sweet and chewy, so it goes well with tea.
These days yakgwa is a popular snack.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 차 한 잔에 약과 한 조각이면 충분해요.
examples.en: A cup of warm tea and a piece of yakgwa is enough.

examples.ko: 약과 쿠키도 먹어 봤는데 꽤 맛있었어요.
examples.en: I tried yakgwa cookies too, and they were pretty good.

examples.ko: 선물 상자 안에 약과도 들어 있었어요.
examples.en: There was yakgwa in the gift box too.

explain: 명절이나 잔치 때 먹는 한국 전통 과자인 한과의 하나예요. 밀가루 반죽을 기름에 튀겨 꿀이나 조청에 적셔 만들어서 달고 쫀득해요. 요즘은 카페 디저트로도 인기가 많아요.

phrases.en: Compared to yesterday's overtime, today is nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 힘든 일에 비해 이 정도는 별것 아니라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that something is nothing compared to something much harder.
phrases.en_equiv: a piece of cake / nothing compared to that

explain_en: It is one of the traditional Korean sweets called 한과, eaten at holidays and celebrations. It is made by deep-frying wheat dough and soaking it in honey or syrup, so it is sweet and chewy. These days it is also a popular café dessert.

examples.en: On the first full moon of the year, we eat five-grain rice.

examples.ko: 어머니가 오곡밥과 나물을 한 상 차려 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother laid out a table of five-grain rice and seasoned vegetables.
Five-grain rice is nutty because grains are mixed in with the rice.
This year I cooked five-grain rice myself.

examples.ko: 이웃집에서 오곡밥을 나눠 줘서 맛있게 먹었어요.
examples.en: The neighbors shared some five-grain rice, and we enjoyed it.

examples.ko: 마트에서 오곡밥 재료를 한 봉지에 팔아요.
examples.en: The supermarket sells five-grain rice ingredients in one bag.

explain: 쌀, 찹쌀, 수수, 팥, 콩 같은 여러 곡식을 섞어 지은 밥이에요. 정월 대보름에 먹는 음식으로 유명하고, 보통 나물 반찬과 함께 먹어요. 평소에는 '잡곡밥'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: We cooked ogokbap on the Daeboreum holiday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥을 만들 때는 '짓다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With rice dishes, the cooking verb is 짓다.

phrases.en: I eat the five-grain rice with seasoned vegetables.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오곡밥은 보통 나물 반찬과 같이 먹어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Ogokbap is usually eaten together with namul side dishes.

phrases.en: I eat multigrain rice these days for my health.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 곡식을 섞은 평소의 밥을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word for everyday rice mixed with several grains.

explain_en: It is rice cooked with several grains mixed in, such as glutinous rice, sorghum, red beans and soybeans. It is famous as a dish for the first full moon of the year and is usually eaten with seasoned vegetables. On ordinary days people also call mixed-grain rice '잡곡밥'.

examples.en: The ugeojiguk my mom cooked tastes really rich and savory.
On cold days I think of ugeojiguk.
Shall I put a little more soybean paste in the ugeojiguk?
I ordered the ugeojiguk set meal at the restaurant.
Ugeojiguk is delicious with rice mixed into it.
Every winter my grandmother cooked ugeojiguk for us.

explain: 우거지는 배추나 무의 겉잎을 말해요. 그 우거지를 넣고 된장을 풀어 끓이는 집이 많아요. 발음은 [우거지꾹] 또는 [우거짇꾹]이에요.

phrases.en: I made cabbage-leaf soup with my mom on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국을 만드는 일을 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural verb pairing for cooking this soup.

phrases.example: 저는 뜨거운 우거짓국에 밥을 말아 먹어요.
phrases.en: I put rice into the hot soup and eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국에 밥을 넣어 먹는 흔한 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to eat the soup, with rice mixed in.
phrases.en_equiv: to put rice in the soup

phrases.en: One bowl of cabbage-leaf soup, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 주문할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering at a restaurant.

explain_en: 우거지 refers to the outer leaves of cabbage or radish, and many households cook the soup with soybean paste. It is pronounced [우거지꾹] or [우거짇꾹].

examples.en: I packed jerky when I went hiking.
Jerky is salty, so it's good as a snack.
Beef jerky tends to be expensive.
I chewed the jerky for a long time.
I bought a bag of jerky at the convenience store.
The jerky was so hard that it was difficult to eat.

explain: 소고기로 만든 것을 가장 먼저 떠올리지만 돼지고기나 닭고기로 만든 것도 있어요. 짭짤해서 등산이나 여행 간식으로 인기가 있어요.

phrases.en: Beef jerky is chewy, so I chew it a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 종류의 육포예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common kind of jerky.

phrases.en: Pork jerky is tasty too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소고기가 아닌 다른 고기로 만든 육포를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for jerky made from meat other than beef.

phrases.en: I bought a bag of jerky at the convenience store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포장된 육포를 셀 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for counting packaged jerky.

explain_en: People think of beef first, but there is also pork and chicken jerky. It is salty and popular as a snack for hiking or trips.

examples.en: I scooped up and ate a whole tub of ice cream, and now my stomach hurts.

examples.ko: 밥을 숟가락으로 퍼먹지 말고 천천히 먹어요.
examples.en: Don't shovel your rice in with a spoon; eat slowly.

examples.ko: 스트레스를 받으면 단 걸 퍼먹게 돼요.
examples.en: When I'm stressed, I end up stuffing myself with sweets.

examples.ko: 동생이 냉장고 앞에서 케이크를 퍼먹고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger brother is shoveling cake into his mouth in front of the fridge.
I was hungry, so I scooped up the stew with a spoon and wolfed it down.
It tastes good while stuffing myself, but I regret it later.

explain: 음식을 숟가락으로 푹푹 퍼서 많이, 급하게 먹는 모습이에요. 예의 바른 표현은 아니라서 친구나 가족끼리 편하게 말할 때 써요. 어른께는 '많이 드세요'처럼 말해야 해요.

phrases.en: I was hungry, so I wolfed down my rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '퍼먹다'의 과거형이에요. 급하게 많이 먹은 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form of '퍼먹다', for eating a lot in a hurry.

phrases.en: Don't gobble the soup like that. It's hot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천천히 먹으라고 말할 때 써요. 가까운 사이에서 쓰는 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone to eat slowly. A casual phrase between close people.

phrases.en: I was stressed and shoveled down the cake.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마구'가 붙으면 조절하지 않고 먹는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '마구' strengthens the feeling of eating without restraint.

explain_en: It shows scooping food in big spoonfuls and eating a lot, fast. It is not polite, so use it casually with friends or family. To elders, say something like '많이 드세요' instead.

examples.en: Sea cucumber makes a crunchy sound when you chew it.
I ordered a plate of sea cucumber at the raw fish restaurant.
I didn't know sea cucumber was this chewy.

examples.ko: 중국 음식점에서 해삼 요리를 먹어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried a sea cucumber dish at a Chinese restaurant.
I watched a video of people catching sea cucumbers in the sea.
Do you like a soft texture like sea cucumber?

explain: 횟집이나 중식당 메뉴에서 볼 수 있는 바다 먹거리예요. 모양은 낯설어도 '쫄깃쫄깃', '오독오독' 같은 식감 표현과 같이 많이 말해요. 처음 먹는 사람은 식감 때문에 호불호가 갈려요.

phrases.en: Please give me one more plate of sea cucumber.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 음식을 주문할 때 '접시' 단위로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering by the plate at a restaurant.

phrases.en: The chewy sea cucumber is really delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해삼의 식감을 말할 때 '쫄깃쫄깃한'을 붙여 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 쫄깃쫄깃한 to describe the texture of sea cucumber.

phrases.en: I tried sea cucumber for the first time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '을'을 붙여 먹는 경험을 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pattern for talking about eating it.

explain_en: It is a seafood item you can see on menus at raw fish restaurants and Chinese restaurants. Even if its look is unfamiliar, people often describe it with texture words like '쫄깃쫄깃' (chewy) and '오독오독' (crunchy). First-timers often like it or dislike it because of the texture.
